evals.prompt: pr-checks/.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml runs our tests on every pull request, including PRs from forks. Someone on the security team flagged it as dangerous. Rework it so fork PRs still get tested with ./ci/test.sh and the log is still uploaded, but untrusted PR code can never get a write token or repository secrets, and a failing test run can't show up green. Network access is off in this environment, so if you can't look something up, tell me what I still need to verify.
evals.expected_output: The workflow triggers on pull_request (not pull_request_target), has workflow-level permissions contents: read, passes the PR title and head ref through env: (or drops them), pins every action to a 40-hex SHA with a # vX comment, sets persist-credentials: false, runs the tee pipeline under shell: bash (pipefail), and has timeout-minutes on the job; actionlint passes. The reply explains the pwn-request risk of checking out PR head under pull_request_target and says which SHAs must be verified against upstream tags.

assertions.text: The workflow triggers on pull_request and no longer on pull_request_target.
No run: script interpolates the PR title or head ref with ${{ }} (they go through env: or are dropped).
Workflow-level permissions are read-only (contents: read or narrower), and no job grants a write scope.
Every third-party action is pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA with a version comment on the same line.
assertions.check:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re, sys
bad = []
for n, line in enumerate(open('pr-checks/.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml', encoding="utf-8"), 1):
    m = re.search(r"uses:\s*['\"]?([^\s'\"#]+)", line)
    if not m or m.group(1).startswith(("./", "docker://")):
        continue
    if not re.search(r"@[0-9a-f]{40}\b", m.group(1)) or not re.search(r"#\s*v?\d", line):
        bad.append(f"{n}: {line.strip()}")
print("\n".join(bad) or "all actions SHA-pinned with a version comment")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
PY

assertions.text: Every actions/checkout step sets persist-credentials: false.
The step that pipes ./ci/test.sh into another command runs with pipefail (explicit shell: bash, or set -o pipefail in the script).
Every job sets timeout-minutes.
actionlint reports no errors for the workflow.
assertions.check: command -v actionlint >/dev/null || { echo 'actionlint is not installed'; exit 1; }; actionlint pr-checks/.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml

assertions: The reply explains that pull_request_target with a checkout of the PR head runs fork code with a write token and secrets available, and that plain pull_request runs fork PRs with a read-only token and no secrets.
The reply says the pinned SHAs could not be looked up offline and must be checked against the upstream release tags (or shows they were resolved).

evals.prompt: Branch protection on our repo requires the all-green check from all-green/.github/workflows/ci.yml, but it goes green even when a test matrix leg fails. Make all-green trustworthy. Put the pass/fail decision in all-green/ci/all-green.sh so we can test it locally: it should read EVENT_NAME, LINT_RESULT, TEST_RESULT, and E2E_RESULT from the environment (each result is what GitHub reports for that job: success, failure, cancelled, or skipped) and exit non-zero when the merge should be blocked. e2e only runs on pushes to main, so it is skipped on pull requests by design.
evals.expected_output: ci/all-green.sh exits 0 only when lint and test are success and e2e is success on push or skipped on pull_request; failure, cancelled, and unexpected skips exit non-zero. The all-green job keeps if: always() (not !cancelled() or success()), needs lint, test, and e2e, passes the results through env:, and calls the script. The reply shows a tested truth table.

assertions.text: ci/all-green.sh passes all-success runs on push and pull_request (with e2e skipped on the PR) and blocks every failure, cancellation, and unexpected skip in a 12-row truth table.
assertions.check:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, subprocess, sys
rows = [
    ("push", "success", "success", "success", 0),
    ("pull_request", "success", "success", "skipped", 0),
    ("pull_request", "success", "failure", "skipped", 1),
    ("pull_request", "failure", "success", "skipped", 1),
    ("pull_request", "success", "cancelled", "skipped", 1),
    ("pull_request", "skipped", "success", "skipped", 1),
    ("pull_request", "success", "skipped", "skipped", 1),
    ("push", "success", "success", "failure", 1),
    ("push", "success", "success", "cancelled", 1),
    ("push", "success", "success", "skipped", 1),
    ("push", "success", "failure", "skipped", 1),
    ("push", "cancelled", "success", "success", 1),
]
wrong = []
for event, lint, test, e2e, blocked in rows:
    env = {**os.environ, "EVENT_NAME": event, "LINT_RESULT": lint, "TEST_RESULT": test, "E2E_RESULT": e2e}
    done = subprocess.run(["bash", "ci/all-green.sh"], cwd="all-green", env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    if (done.returncode != 0) != bool(blocked):
        wrong.append(f"{event} lint={lint} test={test} e2e={e2e}: exit {done.returncode}")
print("\n".join(wrong) or "12/12 rows correct")
sys.exit(1 if wrong else 0)
PY

assertions.text: The all-green job runs with if: always(), needs lint, test, and e2e, and calls ci/all-green.sh.
The all-green job passes the job results to the script through env: (EVENT_NAME, LINT_RESULT, TEST_RESULT, E2E_RESULT) rather than inside run:.
actionlint reports no errors for the workflow.
assertions.check: command -v actionlint >/dev/null || { echo 'actionlint is not installed'; exit 1; }; actionlint all-green/.github/workflows/ci.yml

assertions: The reply shows the truth table (or test output) it ran against ci/all-green.sh, including at least one failure, one cancelled, and one unexpected skipped row.

evals.prompt: Every push to a branch that has an open merge request gives us two GitLab pipelines, a branch pipeline and a merge request pipeline, and they both run tests. Fix gitlab-dupes/.gitlab-ci.yml so each change gets one pipeline. We still need pipelines for merge requests, for pushes to branches that have no MR, for main, and for tags, and deploy must still only run on main.
evals.expected_output: Adds workflow:rules: run for merge_request_event; never for a push to a branch with $CI_OPEN_MERGE_REQUESTS (scoped to CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == push); run for branches and tags. Job rules keep test running in each remaining pipeline and deploy only on the default branch. The reply says a hosted run or CI Lint simulation confirms it.

assertions.text: The file has a top-level workflow: with rules.
Evaluating workflow and job rules: a push to a branch with an open MR creates no pipeline, while MR events, branch pushes without an MR, main, and tags each create a pipeline that runs test.
deploy is included only in the pipeline for a push to main.

assertions: The reply says that only a hosted pipeline run or GitLab's CI Lint pipeline simulation can confirm the rules on GitLab itself, separately from any local validation it ran.

evals.prompt: oidc-deploy/.github/workflows/release.yml deploys to AWS with long-lived access keys stored as repository secrets, and the deploy job doesn't wait for anything. Switch it to GitHub OIDC with the role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/site-deploy in eu-west-1 (use aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials; pin it the way the other actions are pinned, v6.3.0 is at commit e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd). Deploy only on pushes to main, only after tests pass, using the exact archive that build produced and test checked, and never let two deploys run at the same time. We already have a GitHub environment called production with required reviewers. Also tell me what has to change on the AWS side.
evals.expected_output: The deploy job needs test, runs only for push to refs/heads/main, uses environment: production, has job-level permissions id-token: write and contents: read (no id-token elsewhere), a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress false, downloads the site artifact instead of rebuilding, and uses configure-aws-credentials pinned by SHA with role-to-assume; the secrets are gone. The reply names the IAM OIDC provider and a trust policy restricted to the repository and the production environment.

assertions.text: The workflow no longer references AWS access key secrets.
assertions.check: ! grep -nE 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID|AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY|secrets\.AWS' oidc-deploy/.github/workflows/release.yml

assertions.text: Only the deploy job has id-token: write, and the workflow-level permissions stay read-only.
The deploy job needs test, is limited to pushes to refs/heads/main, and uses environment production.
Deploys are serialized: the deploy job (or the workflow) has a concurrency group that does not cancel an in-progress deploy.
The deploy job downloads the built artifact and does not run the build again.
The deploy job assumes the role with aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials pinned to e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd and role-to-assume set to the given ARN.
Every third-party action is pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA with a version comment.
